experiments.paper_location: Section 4.3, at-least-two-table candidate selection; repaired alternate table construction
experiments.mechanism: Validate unsorted codes, build bucket prefixes and stable token contents with scoped temporary ownership, then compare fastfill and sorted-fill retrieval independently to literal token-table collisions.

conditions.execution: Portable selected maintained C++ bodies; serial OpenMP; explicit non-owning Torch metadata/buffer shim and portable sorted-fill copy substitute
conditions.seed: Fixed literal/formula integer codes; no randomness
conditions.configuration: K2,L4,2 layers,2 requests,2 KV heads,4 query heads,capacity35; all-colliding and two mixed patterns;2 owner lifetimes;4 replacement generations
conditions.oracle: Enumerate each original token and count distinct matching table coordinates, accepting exactly >=2; sorted-fill parity is supplementary and not the sole oracle
conditions.contract: Allocated owner; valid layer/request; rank3 contiguous CPU int32 [KV heads,L,length]; length within capacity; bucket codes [0,2^K). Whole input validated before owner mutation. Repeat fastfill replaces selected request tables including empty input; copies token IDs, does not borrow hash input.
conditions.sanitizers: Run ASan/UBSan/LSan with leak detection enabled on hosted runner; no expected leak is accepted after repair

experiments.note: Deliberate Issue66 maintained production variant replaces the archived incomplete fastfill behavior; immutable archive remains unchanged. Synthetic metadata validation does not prove Torch ABI, tensor dispatcher or GPU runtime. alloc-once/valid configuration remains a prerequisite; allocation exception guarantees and OpenMP scheduling are outside this suite. Native AVX sorted-fill copy is covered separately by lsh_retrieval.
